full_judgment:
11. It is the case of the plaintiff that Golam Ali Sk. held the raiyati interest under the Glaosh landlord in Khatian No. 188 and under Golam Ali Kohiluddin, defendant No. 1, his brother Fatik father of defendants Nos. 2, 3 and 4 and Yousuf held an under tenancy in Khatian No.188(1). Admittedly the plaintiff could not file any paper to show directly the annulment of this under tenancy in accordance with section 167 of the Bangal Tenancy Act. The learned Advocate for the 5 appellant submits that mere non-production of the notice under section 167 or paper connected with the service of such notice by itself Would not be fatal for the plaintiff's case if it could be proved otherwise that there was service of such notice and the encumbrance was, in fact, annulled. 

 14. The evidence on record also shows that 10 decimals of land in south-east part of plot No. 66 of khatian No. 188(1) was recorded in S.A. khatian sometime in 1960 corresponding to 1367 B.S. This recording was objected to by the plaintiff by filing a petition before Revenue Circle Officer (Ext. 3) whereupon the R.C.C. held a local inquiry and found that 10 decimals of land was recorded in the name of the defendants as-forcible occupier since 1366 B.S.
